content.user_title: Create Structured Product and Technical Specs
content.value_statement: Feature ideas often become inconsistent PRDs, technical specs, and UX specs. This skill turns requirements into ordered, template-based specs with validation checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates PRDs from an existing app vision document.
Creates technical specs from an existing PRD.
Creates UX specs from existing PRD and technical specs.
Enforces the app vision, PRD, tech spec, and UX spec dependency chain.
Uses provided templates for product, technical, and UX document structure.
Runs validation scripts to check structure and dependencies.
limitations: Requires the expected source specs to exist before dependent specs are created.
Does not write or modify application implementation code.
Validation checks structure and dependencies, not business correctness.
Generated specs still need human review for accuracy and feasibility.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn an app vision into a PRD with goals, user stories, requirements, scope, and success metrics.

use_cases.title: Prepare Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Convert an approved PRD into a technical spec covering architecture, APIs, security, testing, and deployment.

use_cases.title: Align Product Design
use_cases.description: Create a UX spec from product and technical specs, including flows, components, accessibility, and responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a product requirements document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD from specs/app-vision.md. Save it to specs/prd.md and run the validation scripts before reporting the result.

prompt_templates.title: Create Technical Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after the PRD exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create technical specs from specs/prd.md. Include architecture, data models, APIs, security, testing, deployment, and implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Create UX Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Create UX specs from specs/prd.md and specs/tech-specs.md. Include flows, components, accessibility, responsive design, and interaction states.

prompt_templates.title: Build Spec Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the full spec chain for this feature. First confirm dependencies, then update PRD, tech specs, and UX specs in order.

output_examples.input: Feature request for AI note autocomplete with an existing app vision.
output_examples.output: A PRD draft with problem statement, goals, user stories, requirements, scope, and success metrics.

output_examples.input: Approved PRD for a prediction dashboard.
output: Technical spec with architecture, APIs, data models, security, testing, and deployment sections.
Completion note with file location, validation status, and next recommended spec.

output_examples.input: Existing PRD and technical spec for a mobile onboarding flow.
output_examples.output: A UX spec covering design principles, screens, responsive behavior, accessibility, motion, and performance targets.

best_practices: Create specs in dependency order: app vision, PRD, technical spec, then UX spec.
Provide concrete feature requirements before asking for a spec.
Review generated specs with product, engineering, and design owners.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a dependent spec before its source spec exists.
Do not use generated specs as final approval without review.
Do not include real secrets, tokens, or production credentials in specs.

faq.question: What documents can this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates PRDs, technical specifications, and UX specifications from existing requirement documents.

faq.question: Does it implement the feature?
faq.answer: No. It only creates planning and specification documents.

faq.question: What input does a PRD need?
faq.answer: A PRD requires an app vision file at the expected specs path.

faq.question: What input does a technical spec need?
faq.answer: A technical spec requires an existing PRD.

faq.question: What input does a UX spec need?
faq.answer: A UX spec requires both the PRD and technical specification.

faq.question: Does the skill validate the output?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs bundled scripts to check document structure and dependency references.
